label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.7 a.1… supports For every being x, if the esse of x is…
note: Q.7 a.1 co. says of God that his esse 'non sit esse receptum in aliquo, sed ipse sit suum esse subsistens', and ad 3 that his esse is 'per se subsistens non receptum in aliquo', and that a subsistent whiteness, 'ex hoc ipso quod non esset in alio', would differ from all whiteness in a subject. The passage asserts both of God and never infers subsistence from non-reception; it does not state the general conditional that whatever has unreceived esse is its own being. The existing claim reads the sentence through a represented essence/esse equality, not through own being.
